description: This image displays three pie charts comparing the distribution of four categories—labeled N-K+, N-K-, N+K-, and N+K-—across three different difficulty levels: “easy,” “medium,” and “CoT.” Each pie chart is segmented into four colored portions corresponding to these categories, as indicated by the legend on the right: teal for N-K+, yellow for N-K-, orange for N+K-, and red for N+K-. The “easy” chart shows a teal slice at 40.6%, a yellow slice at 45.9%, an orange slice at 10.1%, and a red slice at 3.3%. The “medium” chart shows a teal slice at 44.6%, a yellow slice at 44.3%, an orange slice at 7.2%, and a red slice at 3.9%. The “CoT” chart shows a teal slice at 20.1%, a yellow slice at 36.2%, an orange slice at 36.8%, and a red slice at 7.0%. All percentages are explicitly labeled within their respective slices, and the slices are arranged in a clockwise order, generally from largest to smallest within each chart, though not perfectly sorted. The charts appear to be presented without any visual emphasis like exploded slices.
